title: Two lines moving the same way show in the Create invoice window
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure the test location is connected to QuickBooks Online, with Inventory Asset and Cost of Parts mapped on its ShopView Accounts page, and that AccountingHub is not enabled.
  • Make sure Comeback is mapped to account C at the test location.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A.
  • Have a new work order for this test, work order 1, for customer A, in status Complete, billable, whose line 1 and line 2 each hold a special-order part with a vendor bill posted to Cost of Parts ($90.00 and $60.00), then both marked No Charge under Comeback.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 2:

  • "Create invoice [number]?" opens with the move from Cost of Parts to [account C] for line 1 and line 2 ($90.00 and $60.00, $150.00 together), shown as the PO rules.

Words in square brackets in a message stand for the value they name, such as the work order's number or the customer's name exactly as it is saved; every other word of the message must match exactly.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11764 (Story 7, QuickBooks Online sync)

  • S7-R8: “On a billable work order with no-charge lines (Story 12), the invoice is sent to QuickBooks as today with those lines at $0.00. For each no-charge line, the inventory journal entries of its picked stock parts debit the line's category account instead of Cost of Parts, with the same credit, numbering, dating and idempotency as S7-R2 and S7-R6; special orders and sublet on the line follow S7-R3 and S7-R4 with the category account. The billable lines post as today. Invoice reversal reverses them with the rest. The no-charge line is sent on the QuickBooks invoice as a line: the same labor and part items it would carry as a billable line, its quantities, price 0.00, the same tax code (tax is zero on zero), and the category name in the description, so the QuickBooks invoice reads like the PDF. The cost reaches the category account through the journal entry, never through the invoice. Vendor bills per line: a bill entered while the line is No Charge posts the line to the line's category account (S7-R3 per line); a line marked No Charge after its bill posted is reclassed from Cost of Parts to the category account when the customer invoice is created (S7-R4 per line); Mark as Billable after a bill posted to the category account reclasses back to Cost of Parts at invoicing; Create invoice has no confirmation today (SV-10312), so when at least one vendor bill's cost will move at invoicing and the location has an accounting integration, Create invoice first opens "Create invoice [number]?" with one "Moved from [account] to [account]" row per move and the buttons Cancel and "Create invoice"; every other Create invoice runs as today, with no dialog. The Class rule of S7-R2 applies. The API owner confirms how today's $0 statement of a declined line is sent and makes the no-charge line the explicit case.”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Create invoice with a cost move | "Create invoice [number]?" with one "Moved from [account] to [account]" row per move | Confirmation dialog, Cancel / Create invoice; shown only when a vendor bill's cost moves at invoicing and the location has an accounting integration (S7-R8)”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
